# Long context has several axes: position, access, and state compression

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/context-and-state.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-30 · 34 topic entries / 8 representative comparisons

Ask first how history is stored and then how the current token reads it. RoPE changes relative position relationships; Mamba writes history into recurrence; NSA splits access across paths; OpenAttention retains proxies for unread content; and TTR fits an input-conditioned compression. MERLIN keeps routing-key moments beside compressed segment states to change how segments are read without replacing their internal recurrent writes. A single supported-length number cannot rank these designs.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Expressible position is not accessible history

RoPE defines how QK carries relative position, but full attention still processes visible history. Mamba changes storage and propagation, replacing per-token access with state. Position extrapolation failure and forgetting a detail in state are different; extra state alone cannot explain the former and changing positions cannot fix the latter. Identify whether the task needs exact lookup or persistent state updates.

Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### Can compressed history still expose details?

NSA's compressed branch sits beside query-conditioned exact block reads. OpenAttention spends budget on exact rows and leaves the rest in normalization as log-count mean proxies. TTR maps whole groups to regression coefficients with no per-item invertibility guarantee. Trace where missing information goes rather than counting output vectors. Local formulas or short runs do not rank long-text capability.

Sources: [Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention](../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en.md) · [OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en.md) · [Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression](../../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en.md)

### October 29: new methods and evidence boundaries

Select-TTT changes how strongly each context chunk writes to fast weights based on current query token probability mass; apply-before-write preserves temporal order. Clipping can leave the total below the chunk count and must not be renormalized to fake conservation. Sleep separates active learning from offline consolidation; locally only LTI reward runs. Its full method trains added parameters, so the reward operator does not establish memory written into the model.

Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36794-select-ttt/README-en.md) · [Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories](../../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en.md)

### Write state first, then choose which segments to read

Mamba's selective recurrence controls what enters a state; MERLIN assumes compressed segments and readouts already exist and routes the current query among them. Equal key means can hide a few strong matches. Raw second moments recover aligned variance but not missing within-segment detail. Eq. 9 normalizes means and variances separately before mixing, unlike mixing logits then softmax. Equal-length segments and causal visibility are required.

Sources: [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](../../../../foundation-models/2610.37645-merlin/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why are changing RoPE and switching to recurrence not the same fix for a forgotten early one-off identifier? {#cross-position-versus-memory}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** RoPE changes position in QK, not access to original evidence. Mamba changes selective state writing; if it omits the identifier, no original KV remains to query. Diagnose position distortion, invisibility, or compression loss first, then decide whether to use detail access such as NSA.

    **Illustrative example:** An order ID appears once on the contract cover. Correct relative positions do not ensure it is read, and bounded state does not retain every ID.

    Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md) · [Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention](../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en.md)

### How do selected NSA blocks and OpenAttention unread-cluster proxies handle omissions differently? {#cross-tail-proxy-versus-selection}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** NSA gates overview, selected blocks, and recent-window outputs; OpenAttention includes unread clusters as count-corrected proxies in the same attention normalization as exact rows. Multiple coverage paths and tail mass/value approximation can both lose within-group details.

    **Illustrative example:** One outlier among 100 records can be diluted by either a coarse summary or a mean; test whether selection routes it to an exact read.

    Sources: [Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention](../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en.md) · [OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en.md)

### Do TTR input-wise fitting and Mamba per-token state updates mean the deployment model trains its weights? {#cross-input-adaptation-versus-parameter-update}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. TTR solves coefficients in the current group's forward pass using outer-trained targets and regularization. Mamba uses fixed parameters and current tokens to update state. These are input-dependent computation or runtime state, not optimizer updates, and have different solve versus recurrence costs.

    **Illustrative example:** One frozen model can produce different states and coefficients for two texts without writing a new checkpoint.

    Sources: [Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression](../../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### What actual execution is evidenced by query-conditioned write coefficients versus Sleep reward changes? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Local Select-TTT updates a small fast-weight matrix, allowing pre-write outputs and final state checks. Local Sleep returns a reward without an optimizer or parameter expansion. Neither establishes long-context capability, and reward is not long-term retention.

    **Illustrative example:** Updating a memory table and scoring a continuation 0.9 are different evidence.

    Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36794-select-ttt/README-en.md) · [Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories](../../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en.md)

### Does adding a second moment turn MERLIN's bounded Mamba-like state into full attention? {#cross-merlin-routing-not-state-recurrence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The moment estimates alignment variance between the query and each segment's routing keys to combine readouts. Token values remain compressed and are not individually normalized; an added access cue cannot reverse compression.

    **Illustrative example:** Means of 1 do not distinguish a segment of all ones from a segment of −1 and 3. Variance distinguishes them but cannot reconstruct every original record.

    Sources: [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](../../../../foundation-models/2610.37645-merlin/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-10-30** · Reviewed MERLIN Eqs. 7–9: distinguish raw second moments, alignment variance, and two-softmax gated readout from Mamba recurrence; document completed causal segments, the external current segment, and the lack of exact attention.

Affected: [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](../../../../foundation-models/2610.37645-merlin/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

**2026-10-29** · Select-TTT scales fast-weight writes by query token probability mass and preserves apply-before-write order. Do not renormalize the clipped total to the chunk count. Sleep uses distinct active and consolidation stages; only its LTI reward runs here. Unlike frozen-parameter state updates, full Sleep trains extensions, which a reward operator cannot establish.

Affected: [Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36794-select-ttt/README-en.md) · [Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories](../../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en.md)

**2026-10-27** · Initial version: compared position, selective state, three sparse read paths, tail proxies, and forward regression compression by how they preserve and recover history.
